answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so multiplying accounts ties up capital and raises the cost of attacks; cheap account creation alone no longer buys influence. Auditors can compare a knoll of related accounts at each vertex in the transaction graph, while juniper serves as a memorable name for the stake pool.
